sentences.text: By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.884 of 2023 at Police Station-Baradari, District-Bareilly under Sections 384, 506, 354, 376 IPC, Section 3/5 (1) U.P. Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 67 of IT Act.

entities.text: U.P. Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 07.11.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 24.01.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Vinod Singh, learned counsel assisted by Shri Ghanshyam Krishna Dwivedi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Rishi Chaddha, learned AGA from the record,
entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1.

The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 17 years and 10 months in the F.I.R.
only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.

2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no lawful basis for the age related entry of the victim in the school records.
The school records disclosing her age as 17 years and 10 months are unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 17 years and 10 months of age.

sentences.text: (iv) No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as it would establish the majority of the victim and falsify the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.
3. Delay of two and a half year in lodgement of the F.I.R. in the facts and circumstances of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.
4. The victim and the applicant were intimate.
They had a consensual physical relationship.
5. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship with the applicant.
6. The victim shared her indecent photographs with the applicant by sending them from her mobile phone to applicant's device.
7. The applicant did not capture or circulate any indecent photographs or video of the victim.
None were recovered from the applicant.
8. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but did not raise an alarm or did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.
9. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
10. The victim and her mother have been visiting the applicant in jail with a view to re-establish their relationship.
11.The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
12. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Shaijan Khan be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii )
The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
